title: Margins and unit economics
explanation: A campus café wants to know which products actually make money. **Revenue** is what customers pay. **Gross profit** is revenue minus the cost of the product itself. **Margins** turn those into percentages, so products of different sizes can be compared. This is the language of every finance team.

tasks.prompt: In E2:E5, work out each product's revenue: price × units sold.
tasks.answer: =B2*D2 in E2, then copy down to E5

tasks.prompt: In F2:F5, work out gross profit: (price − unit cost) × units sold.
tasks.teach: **Gross profit** = revenue − cost of goods sold (COGS). Per unit, that's price − unit cost.
tasks.answer: =(B2-C2)*D2 in F2, then copy down to F5

tasks.prompt: In G2:G5, work out each gross margin: gross profit ÷ revenue.
tasks.teach: **Gross margin** = gross profit ÷ revenue. It says how many cents of each dollar are left after paying for the product. Tea's margin is highest, even though it sells the least.
tasks.answer: =F2/E2 in G2, then copy down to G5

tasks.prompt: In H2:H5, work out the profit per unit: price − unit cost.
tasks.answer: =B2-C2 in H2, then copy down to H5

tasks.prompt: In E6 and F6, add up the total revenue and total gross profit.
hints: Or copy E6 across to F6.

tasks.prompt: In B9, work out the operating profit: total gross profit − fixed costs.
tasks.teach: **Operating profit** subtracts the costs you pay no matter what you sell, like rent and salaries, called **fixed costs**.
hints: Total gross profit is in F6, fixed costs in B8.

tasks.prompt: Last one: in B10, work out the operating margin: operating profit ÷ total revenue.
hints: Operating profit is in B9, total revenue in E6.

recap: Gross profit is revenue minus product costs, and operating profit also subtracts fixed costs. Margins divide a profit by revenue, so you can compare products and companies of any size.
